name: Minimal Swiss
description: Strict grid layout, generous whitespace, a single accent color, and type-led hierarchy over decoration. Content is the interface.
anti_patterns: Decorative gradients with no functional purpose
More than one accent color competing for attention
Dense copy without a clear type scale

name: Neo-Brutalist
description: Thick borders, hard drop shadows, unapologetic color blocks, and intentionally 'undesigned' typography that reads as confident rather than unfinished.
anti_patterns: Applying brutalist chaos to a form-heavy operational tool
Illegible contrast in the name of 'raw' aesthetics
No underlying grid at all — brutalism still needs structure to read as intentional

name: Glassmorphism
description: Frosted-glass panels (background blur + low-opacity fill + thin light border) floating over a colorful or photographic backdrop.
anti_patterns: Blur applied over another blurred layer, killing legibility
Using it on data-dense tables where borders need to be crisp, not translucent
Low text contrast against a shifting background

name: Soft Corporate Illustrated
description: Rounded corners, pastel-adjacent palettes, and flat illustration used for empty/onboarding states to feel approachable rather than sterile.
anti_patterns: Illustration used as filler instead of communicating state/status
Overly cute copy on a serious action (deleting data, payments)
Pastel-on-pastel with insufficient contrast for body text

name: Dense Terminal / Data Grid
description: Monospace or tabular-figure type, tight row heights, minimal chrome — optimized for scanning many rows of data quickly, not for delight.
anti_patterns: Adding decorative motion to a screen meant for rapid scanning
Insufficient row-to-row contrast making tables hard to track by eye
Icon-only actions with no text label in a tool used by non-power-users

name: Editorial Serif
description: Serif display type, a comfortable reading measure (60-75 characters), generous line-height, and restrained UI chrome that gets out of the way of long-form text.
anti_patterns: Full-width body text with no measure constraint
Sans-serif UI chrome fighting the serif reading type for visual weight
Justified text without hyphenation, causing ragged word-spacing

name: Dark-Mode-Native Pro Tool
description: Designed dark-first (not just a dark theme bolted onto a light design) with elevation expressed through subtle surface lightening rather than shadows.
anti_patterns: Pure black backgrounds causing halation/glow around light text
Reusing light-mode shadow tokens instead of elevation-through-lightness
Saturated accent colors that vibrate against a dark ground

name: Playful Maximalist
description: Multiple saturated accent colors, layered shapes, hand-drawn or wobbly elements, and confident type mixing — energy over restraint.
anti_patterns: More than 3-4 competing accent colors on one screen
Playful chrome around a genuinely high-stakes action (payment, deletion)
No visual hierarchy — everything shouting at once

name: Quiet Luxury
description: Muted neutral palette, a single refined serif or grotesque, ample whitespace, and understated micro-interactions signaling quality through restraint.
anti_patterns: Loud CTAs breaking an otherwise restrained palette
Stock photography that undercuts the premium feel
Overuse of thin font weights at small sizes, hurting legibility

name: Brutal Functionalism
description: System-default-adjacent styling, visible borders and dividers, no unnecessary ornamentation — every pixel earns its place. Common in enterprise back-office tools.
anti_patterns: Mistaking 'no styling' for 'no design decisions' — spacing and alignment still need a system
Default browser form controls left unstyled next to custom components, breaking consistency

name: Gradient Mesh Modern
description: Soft multi-color mesh gradients as hero backdrops, paired with clean neutral UI chrome — the current default 'modern SaaS' aesthetic.
anti_patterns: Gradient text with insufficient contrast against its background
Overusing the gradient inside the product UI itself rather than just marketing surfaces
Gradients that shift hue enough to imply state (success/error) unintentionally

name: Retro-Futurism
description: Chunky geometric type, CRT/scanline textures, neon-on-dark palettes, and skeuomorphic nods to 80s/90s computing — used for distinctive brand personality.
anti_patterns: Scanline/noise textures reducing text legibility below acceptable contrast
Applying the aesthetic to data-entry forms where speed matters more than mood

name: Flat Material
description: Elevation via layered shadows on flat colored surfaces, rounded rectangles, and a defined type/spacing scale — the mainstream mobile-app default.
anti_patterns: Shadow stacking on every element regardless of actual elevation meaning
Overusing FAB (floating action button) pattern for actions that aren't the primary one

name: Monochrome Technical
description: Grayscale-first palette with a single functional accent reserved strictly for primary actions and status — nothing competes with the data.
anti_patterns: Using the single accent color for more than 2-3 purposes, diluting its meaning
Charts that fall back to arbitrary hues instead of a disciplined grayscale+accent ramp

name: Warm Organic
description: Earthy warm neutrals, soft rounded shapes, textured/grainy backgrounds, and humanist type — evokes craft and care rather than tech-forward slickness.
anti_patterns: Low-contrast warm-on-warm text failing accessibility
Grain/texture overlays that degrade on low-end displays or slow rendering

name: High-Contrast Accessible-First
description: Designed from WCAG AA/AAA contrast outward: strong black-on-white or reversed, oversized touch targets, and no reliance on color alone for meaning.
anti_patterns: Adding decorative low-contrast elements that undo the accessible base palette
Icon-only status indicators with no text or pattern fallback

name: Cinematic Immersive
description: Full-bleed imagery/video, oversized display type, minimal UI chrome that recedes so the content itself is the star — used for showcase/portfolio experiences.
anti_patterns: Auto-playing video/motion with no pause control or reduced-motion fallback
Navigation buried so deep the 'immersive' framing hurts usability

name: Component-Library Default (shadcn-adjacent)
description: Neutral gray scale, a single brand accent, 8px spacing grid, subtle 1px borders and small radii — the safe, fast-to-build default for most modern products.
anti_patterns: Shipping the unmodified default palette/spacing as if it were a considered brand decision
Inconsistent radius values across components from mixing library versions

name: Skeuomorphic Revival
description: Soft shadows, subtle textures, and realistic depth cues (buttons that look pressable) — a reaction against flat design for products wanting tactile warmth.
anti_patterns: Depth cues so heavy they slow down visual scanning of lists
Inconsistent light source across shadowed elements

name: Print-Inspired Editorial Grid
description: Multi-column magazine-style grids, pull quotes, and asymmetric image placement adapted to responsive web — for content that benefits from visual pacing.
anti_patterns: Multi-column layouts that don't collapse sensibly on mobile
Pull quotes breaking reading flow with no clear re-entry point

name: AI-Native Conversational
description: Chat-first layout with a persistent input, streaming-text affordances, subtle 'thinking' states, and generous whitespace around message bubbles.
anti_patterns: No visible distinction between streaming and completed responses
Chat input that scrolls out of view on long conversations instead of staying anchored
